sections.h2: What the Callaway County Recorder of Deeds does
sections.html:
This office keeps the public record of land transactions in the county, and a house sale in Callaway County isn't finished until the deed is filed with it. The county's Recorder page covers deeds, deeds of trust, releases, easements, surveys, plats, affidavits, marriage licenses, military discharges and tax liens.

The office is open to public research and keeps transactions in historical order. A seller usually never walks in, since the title company sends the deed over after closing. It still helps to know what the office will and won't accept, because a rejected deed can hold up your payoff.

The recorded deed is the final step of any sale, including a quick cash sale. Cash Home Buyers can explain what the title company will request from the recorder ahead of closing.

The office is in the Historic Courthouse in Fulton, the county seat.

  • Address: 10 E. 5th Street, Fulton, MO 65251
  • Telephone: 573-642-0787
  • Fax: 573-642-1491
  • Hours: opens at 8:00 in the morning, staff stay until 4:30 in the afternoon, and the register shuts at 4:00

The 4:00 register cutoff matters on a closing day. A deed handed over at 4:15 will most likely be recorded the following business day, so ask the title company which day it plans to submit. The same courthouse holds the Collector, Assessor and County Clerk, which makes one trip enough for most questions about a property.

Callaway County sits north of the Missouri River, across from Jefferson City, and Fulton is the seat. Incorporated places are Auxvasse, Fulton, Holts Summit, Mokane and New Bloomfield, with part of Jefferson City on the south side. Several school districts reach into the county, including Fulton 58, North Callaway County R-I, South Callaway County R-II, New Bloomfield R-III, Community R-VI and Jefferson City Public Schools, so look at which one appears on your tax bill before you list.

With only 46 building permits in 2025, new construction competes lightly with existing houses here, which is one reason a straightforward as-is sale of an older home draws steady interest.

State law lets the recorder keep $5 on page one and $3 on every page that follows. A flat $2 statewide increase under Senate Bill 938 took effect August 28, 2026. The bill at the counter runs well above $5, since other statutory fees ride along on each instrument. Call the Callaway Recorder at 573-642-0787 and ask for the fee sheet in force today. Other charges in RSMo 59.310 include:

  • $5 for each extra item when one document releases or assigns more than one item
  • $25 extra when a document doesn't meet the format rules
  • $1 for a certificate and seal, and up to $2 for the first copied page plus $1 for later pages
  • $25 per sheet to record a subdivision plat, and $5 per sheet for a survey of one or more tracts

Nothing in that fee list is priced from the sale amount, so a deed is billed by pages and document type. The title company totals the recording charge on your settlement statement.

RSMo 59.310 lets the Recorder turn away any document that fails its layout rules, so whoever drafts your deed must follow them. The core requirements are brief.

  • Paper is white or pale, twenty-pound stock or heavier, printed single-sided and left unbound.
  • Print runs at eight point or larger in dark ink and must copy cleanly.
  • Page one leaves a blank three-inch strip at the top for the recorder's stamp, with three-fourths of an inch clear on every other edge.
  • Each signature is inked dark and sits above a typed or stamped name.

Under that blank strip, page one has to carry the document title and date, each grantor with marital status, each grantee, required addresses and the legal description. A document that misses these rules can still go on record for an extra $25. Older deeds signed before 2002, certified copies and papers executed abroad escape the format rules altogether.

A rejected document comes back to the person who submitted it with a written reason, so a mistake costs time more than money.

sections.h2: How to search Callaway County land records
sections.html:
You can view recorded documents online at callawaymo.icounty.com. Printing is available through subscriptions at several levels, and you can call the office for the options. The county's records vendor also runs DeedWatch, a notification service that can alert an owner whenever a new document is filed under that name.

That alert is useful if you've inherited a house or share a title with a relative, because it shows a lien, a release or a new deed soon after it is filed. It can also surface a filing you didn't expect before a buyer's title company finds it.

The county also offers free GIS maps for the public, listed on its home page, which help with parcel lines on rural lots outside Fulton.

sections.h2: Other Callaway County offices that matter in a sale
sections.html:
Three more offices share the courthouse at 10 E. 5th Street. Weekday hours are 8 to 4:30, closed on state holidays.

  • The Collector, at 573-642-0747, bills and takes property tax payments. Statements are mailed during the final week of October.
  • The Assessor values more than 26,000 parcels. Real property calls go to 573-642-0768, and personal property to 573-642-0766.
  • The County Clerk handles Board of Equalization appeals.

Assessor field crews gather data in marked vehicles, wear safety vests with body cameras and county ID, and knock first. They take outside photos, may ask about a finished basement or the number of bathrooms, and never ask to come inside. State law puts the Board of Equalization filing cutoff on the second Monday of July, so ask the Clerk each year for the date that applies.

Back taxes or an open lien on the house should go to the title company early, so the payoff appears on the first draft of the settlement. Ask the title company to confirm after closing that the deed was filed and indexed, since the buyer's tax bill follows the recorded owner.

faqs.q: Where is a Callaway County deed filed?
faqs.a: At the Recorder of Deeds, 10 E. 5th Street, Fulton, MO 65251. The register closes at 4:00 in the afternoon. Call 573-642-0787 to ask how to submit it.

faqs.q: What is the Callaway County recording fee?
faqs.a: State law sets $5 and $3 as the recorder's base, other statutory fees are added, and a $2 statewide increase began August 28, 2026. Request the current Callaway fee sheet from the office.

faqs.q: Can I look up a Callaway County deed online?
faqs.a: Yes. Recorded documents can be viewed at callawaymo.icounty.com, and the Recorder sells subscriptions if you want to print them. The office can also explain what each level includes.

faqs.q: Why would the Recorder reject my deed?
faqs.a: The usual reasons are format problems under RSMo 59.310: a margin smaller than three inches at the top of page one, small or faint type, signatures without printed names, or missing grantor and grantee details. The office sends the document back with a written reason.

faqs.q: Is there a Callaway County transfer tax?
faqs.a: The fee list in RSMo 59.310 carries no transfer tax, only charges by page and document type. Confirm the total for your own deed with the Recorder at 573-642-0787 or with your title company.
